title: 355. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Tangent Radius Perpendicularity
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the relationship between a tangent and the radius at the point of tangency.
questions.question: In circle \(O\), line \(l\) is tangent to the circle at point \(T\). What is the relationship between \(OT\) and \(l\)?
questions.explanation: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency. Since \(T\) is the point of tangency and \(O\) is the center, \(OT\) is perpendicular to the tangent line \(l\).
questions.hint: Recall the standard theorem connecting a tangent and the radius at the point of tangency.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the angle formed by a radius and a tangent at the point of tangency.
questions.question: In circle \(O\), line \(PT\) is tangent to the circle at \(T\). What is the measure of \(\angle OTP\)?
questions.explanation:
By the tangent-radius perpendicularity theorem, the radius \(OT\) is perpendicular to the tangent line \(PT\) at the point of tangency \(T\). Therefore,
\[
\angle OTP=90^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Use the fact that a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the distance from the center to an external point using the tangent-radius right triangle.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(5\text{ cm}\). From external point \(P\), a tangent segment \(PT\) of length \(12\text{ cm}\) is drawn. What is \(OP\)?
questions.explanation:
Since \(PT\) is tangent at \(T\), \(OT\perp PT\). Thus triangle \(OTP\) is right-angled at \(T\). Using the Pythagorean theorem:
\[
OP=\sqrt{OT^2+PT^2}=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=\sqrt{25+144}=\sqrt{169}=13\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, \(OP=13\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use the right triangle formed by the radius, the tangent segment, and the line from the center to the external point.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a tangent length using the tangent-radius right triangle.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(6\text{ cm}\). From external point \(P\), \(OP=10\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the tangent segment \(PT\)?
questions.explanation:
Since \(PT\) is tangent at \(T\), \(OT\perp PT\). Therefore, triangle \(OTP\) is right-angled at \(T\). Thus,
\[
PT=\sqrt{OP^2-OT^2}=\sqrt{10^2-6^2}=\sqrt{100-36}=\sqrt{64}=8\text{ cm}.
\]
So the tangent segment is \(8\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use the Pythagorean theorem with \(OP\) as the hypotenuse.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the equal tangent segments property from an external point.
questions.question: From external point \(P\), tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\) are drawn to a circle. If \(PA=7\text{ cm}\), what is \(PB\)?
questions.explanation:
Tangent segments drawn from the same external point to a circle are equal in length. Since \(PA=7\text{ cm}\), it follows that
\[
PB=PA=7\text{ cm}.
\]
questions.hint: Recall the property of tangent segments from a common external point.

questions.concept: Tangent Line from Distance to Center
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a line is tangent to a circle from the distance between the center and the line.
questions.question: A line is \(5\text{ cm}\) from the center of a circle of radius \(5\text{ cm}\). What is the relationship between the line and the circle?

options.label: A
options.text: The line is tangent to the circle.

options.label: B
options.text: The line is secant to the circle.

questions.explanation: A line is tangent to a circle exactly when the perpendicular distance from the center to the line equals the radius. Here the distance is \(5\text{ cm}\) and the radius is \(5\text{ cm}\), so the line is tangent to the circle.
questions.hint: Compare the distance from the center with the radius.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the converse of the tangent-radius theorem to identify a tangent line.
questions.question: In circle \(O\), line \(l\) passes through point \(T\) on the circle, and \(OT\perp l\). What can be concluded about line \(l\)?

options.label: A
options.text: Line \(l\) is a secant of the circle.

options.label: B
options.text: Line \(l\) is tangent to the circle at \(T\).

questions.explanation: The converse of the tangent-radius theorem states that if a line is perpendicular to a radius at its endpoint on the circle, then the line is tangent to the circle at that point. Since \(OT\perp l\) at \(T\), line \(l\) is tangent to the circle at \(T\).
questions.hint: Use the converse of the tangent-radius perpendicularity theorem.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the radius using the angle between two tangents and the distance from the center to the external point.
questions.question: From external point \(P\), tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\) are drawn to circle \(O\). If \(\angle APB=60^\circ\) and \(OP=10\text{ cm}\), what is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation:
The line \(OP\) bisects \(\angle APB\), so \(\angle APO=30^\circ\). Since \(OA\perp PA\), triangle \(OAP\) is right-angled at \(A\). Thus
\[
OA=OP\sin30^\circ=10\times\frac{1}{2}=5\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, the radius is \(5\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Use the right triangle formed by the radius, the tangent, and the line from the center to the external point.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the angle between two tangents from a given central angle.
questions.question: From external point \(P\), tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\) are drawn to circle \(O\). If \(\angle AOB=130^\circ\), what is \(\angle APB\)?
questions.explanation:
Since \(PA\) and \(PB\) are tangents, \(OA\perp PA\) and \(OB\perp PB\). In quadrilateral \(AOBP\), the angles at \(A\) and \(B\) are each \(90^\circ\), so
\[
\angle APB+\angle AOB=180^\circ.
\]
Thus
\[
\angle APB=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Use the right angles formed by the radii and the tangents.

questions.learningObjective: Use the Pythagorean converse to determine whether a segment is tangent to a circle.
questions.question: In circle \(O\) with radius \(5\text{ cm}\), point \(T\) lies on the circle. If \(PT=12\text{ cm}\) and \(OP=13\text{ cm}\), what can be concluded about \(PT\)?

options.label: A
options.text: \(PT\) is tangent to the circle at \(T\).

options.label: B
options.text: \(PT\) is a secant of the circle.

questions.explanation:
Check triangle \(OTP\). Since \(OT=5\), \(PT=12\), and \(OP=13\),
\[
OT^2+PT^2=5^2+12^2=25+144=169=13^2=OP^2.
\]
By the converse of the Pythagorean theorem, \(\angle OTP=90^\circ\). Therefore, \(OT\perp PT\), so \(PT\) is tangent to the circle at \(T\).
questions.hint: Use the converse of the Pythagorean theorem to check whether \(\angle OTP\) is a right angle.
